propositions: The reconciler's cursor unconditionally advances to the newest event in a fetched window, permanently excluding any candidate that failed to vote in that pass, even though retryable failures like timeout should be re-driven in subsequent passes.

Patch-set uploads that trigger review queuing on an events-log event are permanently dropped when the reconciler processes them as a failure, because the event timestamp is then outside all future ?t1= server-side filters.
The backfill reconciler's cursor must use a low-water mark (minimum of newest event time and the oldest retryably-abandoned candidate time) to re-admit abandoned changes in subsequent passes.
The webhook plugin delivers at-most-once (not at-least-once as documented), making the reconciler the only recovery path, which is broken by the unconditional cursor advance.
Queue depth and held-back candidate tracking must be exposed via /health and reconcile_done emissions so agents can distinguish bot-down, queued, running, and silently-dropped states.
